newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees lower 97/98 Argentina grain crops.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees lower 97/98 Argentina grain crops.

text.p: Lower international grain prices and increased emphasis on oilseeds will push Argentina wheat and corn production down in 1997/98 from the last year's high levels, an U.S. agricultural attache said.
In a report dated March 1 that was released in Washington Friday, the attache pegged the 1997/98 Argentina wheat crop at 14.00 million tonnes, down from the 15.50 million tonnes seen for 1996/97.

The attache forecast 1997/98 corn production at 13.00 million tonnes versus 13.50 million tonnes estimated in 1996/97, saying another possible downward factor on production next year could be expansion of the domestic dairy industry.
"Increasing demand for milk in MERCOSUR may result in more corn being converted to silage, reducing grain output," the attache wrote.
The attache predicted Argentina corn and wheat trade should continue strong in the upcoming year, despite lower output.

"Although aggregate production will likely decrease somewhat in the coming year due to lower price incentives, this is the only one of the major factors in this year's success that is expected to change, providing a relatively positive outlook for next year," the attache wrote.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
